governanceNotes: D1 batch 40 (2026-09-23): deferred on three independent grounds. (i) Finding/manifestation identity and direction-reversed (ME-41 phenotype-identity barrier and direction guard; fissured-tongue batch 34, camptodactyly batch 32 precedents): granulomatous rhinitis is the histopathologic nasal-manifestation of underlying disease - the Rimmer and Lund 2023 review of non-eosinophilic granulomatous disease and the unified airway documents that granulomatous and vasculitic diseases of the airway may be part of more widespread systemic disease but can occur in isolation, presenting to the ENT surgeon with vague symptoms that mimic common chronic inflammatory unified-airway conditions such as rhinitis, chronic rhinosinusitis, and asthma, with bloody nasal discharge and crusting suspicious for granulomatous disease requiring clinical findings, serology, imaging, and histology to confirm the diagnosis (PMID 36410993) - the arrow runs from the underlying etiology (granulomatosis-with-polyangiitis, sarcoidosis, rhinoscleroma and other infectious granulomas) to the rhinitis finding, not from the finding to downstream disease; the underlying etiologic identities own that direction (granulomatosis-with-polyangiitis authored two edges this batch). (ii) Duplicate-scope with the edge-bearing chronic-rhinitis identity: the generic rhinitis downstream pathway (chronic-rhinitis already carries its sleep-apnea association) is owned by the plain-rhinitis identity, and routing a parallel 'granulomatous' rhinitis-to-same-target pathway beneath it would duplicate the unified-airway chain (parallel-pathway ban; geographic-tongue-versus-benign-migratory-glossitis synonym-scope precedent). (iii) Zero-record for forward outcomes: no quantified cohort of incident outcomes attributable to granulomatous rhinitis as such (as opposed to its underlying etiologies) was located in this window - sinusitis progression records belong to the infectious or vasculitic parent diagnoses (zero-record guard; the bacterial-rhinitis-to-sinusitis precedent rests on that identity's own cohort evidence). Negative screens recorded: no hearing-loss or pulmonary edge (routes belong to the systemic parent diagnoses); no epistaxis or anosmia symptom edge (symptom-level, constitutive of the finding, wrong-identity guard). Reopening condition: a quantified outcomes cohort for granulomatous rhinitis as an independent clinical entity, or a governance decision to reclassify it as a specific diagnosis identity.
